extension.description: Reviews Heaven CLI commands that send write requests, run request workflows, generate load, or disable TLS verification.
extension.name: Heaven command protection

permissions.description: Identifies `heaven post|put|patch|delete`, which sends a state-changing HTTP request to the active or specified environment. Protected environments prompt a human, but non-interactive agent sessions bypass that review path. exec and xargs launches are blocked by Guard's wrapper floor.
permissions.label: Heaven write request
safer_guidance: Send the equivalent GET request first to confirm the target resource and environment.
Run against a dev or staging environment, or mark the target environment with `heaven env set NAME --protected`.

permissions.description: Identifies `heaven flow FILE.json`, which executes a chain of requests defined in a file, including write methods, with values extracted between steps. exec and xargs launches are blocked by Guard's wrapper floor.
permissions.label: Heaven flow run
safer_guidance: Read the flow file and check every step's method and URL before running it.
Run the flow against a non-production environment first.

permissions.description: Identifies `heaven bench`, which sends many concurrent requests to a target and can overload a service or trigger rate limits. exec and xargs launches are blocked by Guard's wrapper floor.
permissions.label: Heaven bench load test
safer_guidance: Start with a small request count and low concurrency (for example -n 10 -c 2).
Only benchmark systems you own or are authorized to load-test, and avoid production.

action_classes: Heaven request with TLS verification disabled
permissions.description: Identifies Heaven commands run with `--insecure` or `-k`, which skips TLS certificate verification and exposes the request and any credentials to interception. exec and xargs launches are blocked by Guard's wrapper floor.
permissions.label: Heaven request with TLS verification disabled
safer_guidance: Install or trust the correct CA certificate instead of disabling verification.
Never combine --insecure with --bearer, --basic, or other credentials.
